summary: Technical report on two open-weight policy-following safety classifier models fine-tuned from gpt-oss. Reports classification performance (internal multi-policy, OpenAI Mod 2022, ToxicChat), MMMLU multilingual, and baseline chat-mode safety evals (disallowed content, StrongReject, instruction hierarchy, hallucination, BBQ) against the gpt-oss baselines.

framework.name: Preparedness Framework
framework.level_or_determination: No new frontier eval; prior gpt-oss worst-case estimates deemed to cross-apply
framework.quote: we determined that the previous work estimating worst-case scenarios from gpt-oss release cross applies to these new models.

cbrn_bio_chem.finding: No new bio evals; models trained without additional biological data so prior gpt-oss analysis cross-applies.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: were trained without any additional biological or cybersecurity data.

cyber.finding: No new cyber evals; prior gpt-oss worst-case analysis cross-applies.
cyber.quote: were trained without any additional biological or cybersecurity data.

harmful_content_refusal.finding: In chat use, safeguard models perform roughly on par with gpt-oss (within 1-3 points on standard evals), with minor degradations in some production categories.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: Both of the safeguard models generally perform within 1-3 points of the gpt-oss models on the Standard Disallowed Content Evaluation.

jailbreak_robustness.finding: 120b slightly outperforms gpt-oss-120b; 20b underperforms gpt-oss-20b by 1-5 points.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: We find that gpt-oss-safeguard-120b outperforms gpt-oss-120b and gpt-oss-safeguard-20b underperforms gpt-oss-20b by 1-5 points.

evals: Instruction Hierarchy: system prompt extraction, prompt injection hijacking, phrase and password protection
prompt_injection.finding: Safeguard models tend to underperform gpt-oss on instruction hierarchy evals; cause unknown.
prompt_injection.quote: We observe that the gpt-oss-safeguard models tend to underperform their gpt-oss counterparts. More research is needed to understand why this is the case.

honesty_hallucination.finding: Roughly on par with gpt-oss; unrestricted CoT may contain hallucinated content including language not reflecting policies.
honesty_hallucination.quote: Because these chains of thought are not restricted, they can contain hallucinated content

bias_fairness.finding: Both safeguard models outperform gpt-oss counterparts on BBQ.
bias_fairness.quote: Overall, we see both models outperform their gpt-oss counterparts across all metrics.

child_safety.finding: Only sexual/minors rows within disallowed content tables.

self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Self-harm only as disallowed-content categories; some degradation vs gpt-oss on production benchmarks.

multilingual_safety.finding: Multilingual eval is MMMLU capability only, explicitly not a safety or classification eval.
multilingual_safety.quote: Note that these evaluations address performance in a chat setting and do not directly assess performance during content classification with a provided policy.

evals: safety classification performance of the models themselves
system_safeguards.finding: The models are themselves safeguards; report describes how OpenAI's internal Safety Reasoner is deployed with smaller classifiers and asynchronously.
system_safeguards.quote: we use smaller and faster classifiers to determine which content to assess

evals: CoT monitorability (no direct optimization pressure on CoT)
other_safety.finding: No direct optimization pressure on CoT, citing the CoT monitorability position paper.
other_safety.quote: we did not put any direct optimization pressure on the CoT for either of the gpt-oss-safeguard models.

notable_new_eval_methods: Internal multi-policy classification accuracy eval (multiple policies provided simultaneously) (p.3)

self_reported_limitations.text: Standard disallowed-content evals are saturated and no longer provide useful signal; OpenAI plans to stop publishing them.
Dedicated classifiers trained on tens of thousands of labeled samples can outperform gpt-oss-safeguard; the model is compute-intensive.
Chat-mode safety metrics describe a use the models are not intended for; multilingual eval doesn't assess classification performance.

notes: Safety evals here measure misuse as a chat model, not classification behavior. Classification benchmarks recorded as 'other' capability.
